# dsh-service-hub

**Service Hub for DeepSeek Harness** — a sidebar panel that starts, stops, restarts and
monitors the

local services, one-shot scripts and terminal tools you keep on your own
machine, so you no longer
have to remember where each launcher lives.
## Self-contained since 0.3.0

The package ships its own **zero-dependency console daemon** (`console/`, Node standard
library only

). Installing the plugin is enough: the Host side starts the daemon on
`127.0.0.1:3999` when the plu

gin activates, and stops it when the plugin unloads.
No external tool, no machine-specific path, not

d stops it when the plugin unloads.
No external tool, no machine-specific path, nothing to download.

Registry data and logs live in `~/.dsh-service-hub/`, so upgrading or reinstalling the
plugin keeps

logs live in `~/.dsh-service-hub/`, so upgrading or reinstalling the
plugin keeps your service list.
## What you get

The session header gains a **⚙ 服务** button that opens the **Service** panel, listing
every registere

d entry with live status, health, port and a quick access URL, plus
**start / stop / restart / logs

/ refresh** buttons and a LAN address you can open from a
phone. Services you start keep running whe

n the panel is closed, because the daemon owns
the process control. Installing `dsh-better-sidebar`

also puts the same panel in the
sidebar.
## Install
`dsh-service-hub` is not published on npm yet, so install it from this repository:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`desktop` is the profile the DeepSeek Harness desktop app boots; use the profile you
actually run in

stead (`web` for the web UI, or your own profile name). The desktop
profile must have been started o

nce, and the app must be fully quit while the command
runs. When `dsh` is not on `PATH`, call the co

py the app ships at
`<install dir>/resources/runtime/cli/bin/dsh.cmd`.

Then start DeepSeek Harness again and open the panel from **⚙ 服务** in the session
header.
Once the npm package is published, the short form works as well:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Check the result with `dsh plugin --profile <profile> why dsh-service-hub`. The panel
talks to the c

onsole on `http://127.0.0.1:3999`; the registry and logs live in
`~/.dsh-service-hub/`.
## Requirements
| Requirement | Why |

| DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1+ with the Web/Desktop UI | Client bundle targets `platform: web` |
| Node 1

8+ | Runs the bundled console daemon (the desktop app ships one) |
| Windows | Process management us
es PowerShell and `tasklist`/`netstat` |

`dsh-better-sidebar` is optional: it
adds the same panel as a sidebar tab, which the session-header
button opens anyway.

Port `3999` must be free. If another console already listens there, the plugin reuses it
instead of
starting a second one.
## Permissions and external services

- The client bundle only performs `fetch` against `http://127.0.0.1:3999` (localhost).
- The bundled

daemon binds `127.0.0.1` only, never a public interface.
- No telemetry, no outbound network calls

from the plugin itself.
- The daemon starts and stops processes that **you registered**; it does not

run anything
on its own. Each entry's command is visible in the panel and stored in
`~/.dsh-service
-hub/data/registry.json`.
## Compatibility

- DSH: `>=0.2.1`
- UI: Web / Desktop (session-header panel, optionally a sidebar tab); no effect on

the
TUI or headless profiles
- OS: Windows
## Known limitations
- The panel opens from the session header (⚙ 服务). Installing `dsh-better-sidebar` additionally adds

the same panel as a left sidebar tab; it is optional.
- Panel text is currently Chinese only; `local

e/` ships `meta.title` /
`meta.description` in English and Chinese for the plugin inventory.
- Conso
le URL is fixed to `127.0.0.1:3999`.
### Discovery tries to classify each candidate

`Scan` lists unregistered executables and listening ports. Every candidate carries a
suggested kind

before you add it — `app` for install-directory programs and shortcuts,
`service` for programs that

listen on a port, `terminal` for command wrappers in npm or
user bin directories, `script` for other

batch files — and the discovery dialog shows a
kind selector, so the guess is always overridable. S

ystem directories (`C:\Windows\...`)
are skipped.
## Security
The bundled console listens on `127.0.0.1` only and is guarded against drive-by use:

- **No CORS headers.** Browser requests from any other origin fail at preflight, so a
random website

cannot read `/api/state` or call mutating endpoints.
- **Origin / Sec-Fetch / Host guard.** Script-

initiated cross-site requests get `403`;
top-level and iframe navigation stays allowed so the panel

can embed the page.
- **Safe ids.** Entry ids are limited to `[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}` and every log pa

th is
resolved inside the log directory, so `/api/items/<id>/logs` cannot read other files.
- **`/he

althz`** exposes only `{ ok, version, pid }` plus the `X-LC-Daemon` header, which
the Host uses to c

onfirm it is talking to this plugin's daemon and not an unrelated
process that happens to occupy por

it is talking to this plugin's daemon and not an unrelated
process that happens to occupy port 3999.

The daemon can start and stop the commands **you registered**; it never runs anything on
its own. Ru
n `npm test` to see the regression suite for these guarantees.
## Layout
The console is this plugin. There is no separate project to install or keep in sync:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Data and logs live in `~/.dsh-service-hub/`, so the console, the sidebar panel and a
manually starte

d instance all read the same registry.
